question: Is the 2014 Marikina Pterygoplichthys ovary-morphology paper an independent sample from the 2016 five-station life-history paper, or do they report the same female cohort?

source.title: Ovary Morphology and Reproductive Features of the Female Suckermouth Sailfin Catfish, Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus (Weber 1991) from Marikina River, Philippines
source.citation: Jumawan, J. C., & Herrera, A. A. (2014). Ovary morphology and reproductive features of the female suckermouth sailfin catfish, Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus (Weber 1991) from Marikina River, Philippines. Asian Fisheries Science, 27(1), 75–89. https://doi.org/10.33997/J.AFS.2014.27.1.006
source.accessMethod: Reviewed the official Asian Fisheries Society article page and the author-uploaded full-text copy on ResearchGate, including the abstract, methods, results, station description, discussion, and copyright statement. The official publisher PDF link timed out in the review browser. No article PDF, figure, station map, table, or raw observations were retained.
source.copyrightAndReuse: The full-text copy states © Asian Fisheries Society, and the publisher page does not identify an article-specific open reuse license. This review records citation, methods, and cohort-linkage facts only; no article text, figure, map, table, or measurements are redistributed.

studyDesign.sourceReportedTaxon: Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus (Weber 1991), as labeled by the article; source identity is not independently resolved.
studyDesign.gearAsReported: Cast net, 5 m long with 3.8 cm mesh.
studyDesign.stationAllocation: The article names five study sites but gives no site-by-site fish counts or female-to-station allocation. The site map is not digitized or treated as coordinate data.
studyDesign.voucherAndAccessionStatus: No specimen voucher, catalogue number, GenBank accession, or individual record identifier was found in the reviewed full text.
studyDesign.studyPurpose: Describe ovarian histomorphology, maturity stages, oocyte size distribution, and reproductive timing in source-labeled female Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus.
studyDesign.sourceIdentityCaveat: The article discusses intermediate abdominal patterns and cites Marikina DNA-barcode work that did not establish defined species-specific barcode groups. Preserve P. disjunctivus as this paper’s source label, not an independently reidentified species.

matchingAttributes: Both papers report a July 2010–June 2011 Marikina River collection period.
Both describe the same five named stations: San Jose/Rodriguez, Banaba/San Mateo, Tumana, Malanday, and River Park.
Both report the same cast-net specification: 5 m length and 3.8 cm mesh.
The 2014 ovary paper reports 607 females; the 2016 paper reports 607 females and 526 males for 1,133 total fish.
The 2016 paper explicitly cites Jumawan and Herrera (2014) histological analyses when describing its 499-female GSI subset.
cohortCrosswalk.conclusion: High-confidence publication-level crosswalk: the 2014 female ovary dataset is the female component of, or directly overlaps with, the 2016 607-female/526-male collection. The identical female total, period, five sites, gear, author overlap, and explicit 2016 citation to the 2014 histology support treating the papers as one female cohort for counting, not two independent surveys.
cohortCrosswalk.individualSpecimenLimit: Neither paper provides a specimen-level identifier crosswalk proving that all 607 individual females are identical. Retain this as a high-confidence cohort-level match, not an individual voucher reconciliation.
cohortCrosswalk.countDecision: Count the 607 female field-sampled cohort once. Do not add another 607 females to the 2016 total of 1,133, and do not treat the two publications as independent site-presence confirmations.

taxonomyAndOccurrenceDecision.relationship: The 2011 COI study reports a separate 36-fish Marikina sample and unresolved P. pardalis/P. disjunctivus/intermediate patterns. No voucher or accession connects that series to the 607 females.
taxonomyAndOccurrenceDecision.decision: Keep the 2014/2016 source label at Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus only as an attributed publication label. The 607-female aggregate and five-site study design are not a station-specific occurrence dataset; no coordinates, voucher identifiers, or site-level counts were recovered.

evidenceDecision.decision: Register the 2014 article as a related analysis of the 2010–2011 Marikina female cohort, not a second independent sample. Crosswalk the 607 female aggregate to the 2016 collection once and retain the source taxon label as unresolved research context.

nonClaims: The 2014 paper and the 2016 paper are not two independent sets of 607 female fish; available evidence strongly indicates a shared female cohort, while individual-level identity is not proven.
Neither article provides station-specific sample counts, so the 607 females cannot be allocated among the five sites or assigned to NCR/Rizal separately.
Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus remains a source-reported name, not a specimen-verified identification for the 607 females.
The 2011 barcode series is a separate 36-fish sample and is not used to identify or duplicate the 607 female cohort.
No current occurrence, abundance, catchability, legal status, food/water safety, diet guidance, map geometry, or public app row follows from this cohort crosswalk.
nextActions: Preserve the 2014/2016 607-female sample as one research cohort in any future regional tally.
Do not import station-by-species counts or coordinates from the published station map; require a source-provided sample-to-station dataset.
Resolve the Pterygoplichthys species label only with specimen-level voucher or diagnostic sequence evidence tied to the 607 females.
